notes: Installed version 2.6.13; the source code is closed and has never been published, so the record here is the maker's documentation repository plus the installed binary, which is unstripped and carries a named function per model. The documentation was read at tag v2.6.13 of github.com/DomiKamu/OhmerPrems, not at the branch head: the head README describes 2.6.13 stable alongside a 2.6.14 alpha, and by then the 6OP-DX module had been renamed DeXtral and given a different manual, so the head documents a module that is not the one installed. At v2.6.13 the repository holds a README and five manuals: FranKe, FroeZe, KlokSpidMkII, Vektor, and a nine-line placeholder for 6OP-DX. KordZ and QuadPercs have no manual anywhere; QuadPercs is described control by control in the README and KordZ is not described at all, so its entry is read out of the binary. PANEL THEMES, SETTLED ONCE: every module except the KX and VX expanders carries a Model submenu offering six or eight finishes - Creamy or Aluminium, Stage Repro, Cobalt, Absolute Night, Dark, Fort Knox, Oxide, Deepblue and Titanium Signature, the Signature ones with gold jacks, buttons and screws instead of silver. A new module comes up as Absolute Night when Rack's View menu has Use dark panels if available ticked and as Creamy or Aluminium when it does not. It changes nothing but appearance, so under the house rule it gets no line on any of the eleven, and there is no blank panel here to make the exception. Attached expanders take their parent's model and display brightness rather than having their own. EVERY MODULE'S MENU ALSO ENDS IN A GREYED LICENCE LABEL, either License: full version (for everyone) or a Free/Demo line with the limitations in brackets. It is a label rather than an item and gets no menu line, but where a missing licence actually silences or locks the module - FranKe, FroeZe and its two expanders, QuadPercs - that is written as a Note, because it is exactly the thing that makes a module look broken. KlokSpid MkII, KX, KordZ, Vektor, VX and 6OP-DX are free for everyone and have no such limit. ONE MODEL IS HIDDEN: 6OPDX is marked "hidden": true in the installed plugin.json and so is absent from the module browser. Nothing else in the registration hides anything, and the KlokSpid from the separate free Ohmer plugin that was flagged earlier is not this one - the KlokSpid MkII here carries no hidden flag and is listed normally. A FURTHER COMMON SHAPE: FranKe, FroeZe, KlokSpid MkII, Vektor and 6OP-DX are each worked through a large custom display, which in Rack is a single widget with no ParamWidget per element. None of what is on those screens can be reached by clicking for help, so each of those entries carries a Note saying what the screen is for and how it is worked. Where a module also has a physical joystick or a grid of touch cells, the same applies. Read with the census slice at research/help/census/OhmerPrems.json, the panels rendered from the VCV library screenshot service at 400 pixels, and otool -tvV over the installed plugin.dylib.

lines: An eight-track, sixteen-step, sixty-four-pattern step sequencer with pitch, gate and velocity jacks per track; a track holds quantised notes, free voltages, or a sixteen-bit Turing machine
Drives the sequencer from an outside clock, either as pulses at 32 or 24 PPQN or as a BPM-CV voltage, whichever the SETUP page names; a BPM-CV reading is scaled like 1V per octave, so 0V is 120 BPM
Starts and pauses the sequencer, as a toggling trigger or while a gate is held, whichever the SETUP page names
A trigger sends every track back to the start of its sequence
While a gate is held here, every track plays backwards; a track already set to play backwards plays forwards instead
While a gate is held here, melodic and voltage tracks play to the last step and back again; Turing machine tracks ignore it
The SETUP page chooses what this jack does, from the selected Turing machine track's randomise-and-lock, voltage scale, octave, gate length, delay and speed; in step recording it records velocity
What this jack does is chosen on the SETUP page, from a list covering previous pattern by trigger, track select, and mute, unmute, solo or unsolo a track by voltage of one volt per track
Selects the pattern by voltage over 0V to +10V, which stops the pattern knob from working; when CV2 is set to previous pattern this jack takes a trigger for the next pattern instead
Starts and pauses the sequencer
Starts a step-recording session, in which the buttons down the left edge become piano keys and each press writes a note and moves on one step; it does nothing on a Turing machine track
Sends every track back to the start of its sequence, with no trigger sent from the cycle outputs
Reverses the playing direction of the selected track only
Makes the selected track play to its last step and back again; a Turing machine track does not take it
Opens editing of the per-step velocity on the selected melodic track
Opens editing of the per-step gate length, as a percentage, on the selected melodic or voltage track
Opens editing of which steps of the selected melodic or voltage track are skipped; the logic keeps at least one unskipped step
Opens editing of the per-step subdivision on the selected melodic or voltage track
Opens editing of the per-step chance of being played, as a percentage, on the selected melodic or voltage track
Steps the selected track's role round from melodic to voltage to Turing machine and back
Opens editing of the first and last step of the selected track, which are then set with the STEP 1 and STEP 2 encoders
Opens and closes the module's SETUP page, and ends a step-recording session
Puts all eight tracks of the current pattern into the same mute state in one press
Takes every track of the current pattern out of solo
Selects the pattern, unless a voltage is patched into the PATTRN. jack
Selects that track and, turned, sets the value shown on that track's display; on the SETUP page the encoder on each row changes that row's setting
Sets the note, voltage or Turing machine value of that step on the selected track, and sets the first or last step while STEPS is open
Locks every Turing machine sequence at one press
Carries that track's pitch as 1V per octave when the track is melodic or a Turing machine, and the sequenced voltage between -10V and +10V when the track is a voltage track
Goes to +10V while that track's step is sounding and 0V between steps
Carries the velocity of that track's note, 0V to +10V, on a melodic track, and a +10V 1ms trigger at the start of each pass through the sequence on a voltage or Turing machine track
Note — the sequencer will not advance without a clock. Patch a clock into CLOCK, or it falls back to the last tempo it read, 120 BPM on a new module, and that internal tempo cannot be set by hand.
Note — the eight track displays are touchscreens and the note grid is edited on them; no part of that can be clicked for help, because each display is one widget rather than a control per step
Note — the gear button opens the SETUP page, which sets the clock type, the RUN jack behaviour, the CV1 and CV2 assignments and the flat-or-sharp preference; each track's encoder changes that row
Note — while step recording is running, the REV. jack takes pitch, the PENDUL. jack takes gate and the CV1 jack takes velocity, so a MIDI-to-CV module can play the notes in.
Note — without an OhmerPrems licence keyfile a new module reaches patterns 01 and 02 only, edits tracks 1 and 2 only, and sends a constant -10V from the pitch outputs of tracks 3 to 8.
Note — clicking the Ohmer logo dims or brightens every display on models that have lit ones.
Note — the module cannot be saved as a Rack preset or module selection file; use Sequencer, Pattern and Track in its own menu to write its state to separate files.
Menu — Sequencer: Open, Save as — reads or writes the whole sequencer, every pattern and track, as one file
Menu — Pattern: Open, Save as, Copy, Paste, Move, Swap, Initialize, Insert, Remove — the operations on one pattern of the sixty-four; Copy is greyed while the sequencer runs
Menu — Track: Open (use/set saved track role), Open (keep current track role), Save as, Copy, Paste, Move up, Move down, Initialize, Randomize — the operations on the selected track

3.why: docs/modules/FranKe/Manual.md, INPUT JACKS: held +10V gate; monophonic as above

FranKe.notes: Source is not published; read against the maker's manuals at tag v2.6.13 and against the installed binary, which is unstripped. Every parameter is configured with an empty name, so the panel render and the census positions are the only guide to what each control is; the thirteen buttons down the left edge match the thirteen listed in the manual's LEFT-SIDE MOMENTARY BUTTONS section in the same order. Params 39 and 40 are the two buttons wired by silkscreen to the M and S boxes of the bottom row. FranKeModule::process at 0x83be0 reads param 39 and writes one repeated byte over all eight of the current pattern's mute flags, then calls checkMuteStates; at 0x83fe8 it reads param 40 and writes eight zero bytes over the solo flags, then calls checkSoloStates. The solo button is therefore certainly an unsolo-everything, and the mute button certainly writes one state to all eight; the byte it writes is only ever set to 1 in the reset paths, which suggests a mute-all rather than a toggle, and the line is worded not to claim a direction. The pattern-CV and CV1/CV2 role wordings come from the SETUP hint strings in the binary rather than from the manual, which does not list them.

lines: A sixteen-track, sixty-four-step drum sequencer of 128 patterns: fifteen instrument tracks and an accent track, run from an outside 32 PPQN clock, sending triggers or its own drum machine audio
Takes the clock, which must be 32 pulses per quarter note; the panel prints X32 above the jack because that is the multiplier to set on the clock module
A trigger starts or pauses the sequencer
A trigger sends the pattern back to its first step
Shifts the last step up or down from the number set by the LAST STEP encoder, by voltage
While +2V or more is held here every playing track repeats: +2V to +5V the current step, +5V to +9.99V two steps, +10V the bar. The LOOP button does nothing while this jack is high
While +2V or more is held here, the pattern plays backwards
While +2V or more is held here, the pattern plays to the last step and back again; it is ignored while LOOP is active
Sets the swing applied to the even steps of the whole pattern, 50% and no swing at 0V rising to 75% at +10V; the FroeZe-SX expander switches this jack off
A trigger steps back one pattern. With the NEXT jack empty this jack instead takes a 0V to +10V voltage and selects the pattern outright
A trigger steps on one pattern
Selects the drum machine for the selected instrument track, which matters when the outputs are set to Audio Engine
Selects the kit piece within that drum machine for the selected instrument track; the choice offered follows the nature of the track
Selects the pattern, one of 128
Sets the last step of the pattern, from 1 to 64; with tracks soloed it sets the last step of those tracks alone, which is how polyrhythms are built
Starts and pauses the sequencer
Sends the pattern back to its first step
Repeats the playing step or bar while held; how much is repeated is set by the "LOOP" button behavior menu, and the button does nothing while +2V or more is held on the LOOP jack
Plays the pattern backwards while held
Carries that track's steps as a +10V 1ms trigger, or its drum machine audio when the Outputs menu is Audio Engine; an accented step sends -10V unless the FroeZe-X expander is attached
Carries the accent track's own steps as a +10V 1ms trigger
Note — nothing plays until a 32 PPQN clock reaches the CLK jack; with none patched the black NO CLOCK indicator blinks and the timing of the displays goes erratic.
Note — the grid is worked like a touchscreen: a left click on an empty cell writes a note, a second click accents it, a third makes it a ratchet, and Ctrl or Command with a left click empties it
Note — a left click on a track name selects that track and a second left click solos it; a right click selects it and a second right click mutes it. Solo and mute belong to the pattern
Note — clicking the Ohmer logo dims or brightens every display, on the module and on any attached expander.
Note — a right-side FroeZe-X expander gives the accents their own sixteen output jacks, in place of the -10V the main outputs otherwise send for them, and adds pattern and track editing.
Note — a left-side FroeZe-SX expander gives each instrument track its own swing CV and switches off the %SWING jack on this module.
Note — without an OhmerPrems licence keyfile only the BD, SD, CH, OH and AC tracks and pattern 1 can be edited, and five drum machines sound: Oberheim DMX, Drumulator, LinnDrum, 707 and 808
Menu — Outputs: Triggers (default), Audio Engine (QuadPercs sounds) — chooses whether the sixteen jacks send triggers or the drum machine audio of the internal QuadPercs engines
Menu — "LOOP" button behavior: 1/16 step repeat (default), 1/8, 1/4 beat repeat — sets how much of the pattern the LOOP button repeats
Menu — File — holds Open and Save as for three things: Pattern, Drum Kits and Ratchet slots
Note — a right click on a grid cell opens an on-screen menu for that cell; no part of the grid can be clicked for help, because the whole grid is one widget

FroeZe.notes: Source is not published. Read against docs/modules/FroeZe/Manual.md and the README at tag v2.6.13, and against the unstripped binary. The four unnamed encoders are identified from the rendered panel: DM and KIT across the top, LAST STEP and PATTERN below them; the four named buttons sit in the boxed transport row. The module's own menu is Model, File, Outputs and "LOOP" button behavior; Model is the plugin-wide theme submenu and gets no line. The README describes a "CV PATTERN" context-menu option, and no such item exists in the 2.6.13 binary: what the build actually does is take an absolute pattern voltage on the PREV. jack whenever NEXT is unpatched, which is what the manual's own pattern-change paragraph says.

lines: A 12HP expander for the FroeZe sequencer, placed immediately to its right: it gives every track its own accent output jack and adds pattern and track editing pages.
Carries the accents of that track: a +10V 1ms trigger on each accented step, or a gate held for as long as the drum sample plays when FroeZe's outputs are set to Audio Engine
Carries the accent track's own events as a +10V 1ms trigger
Sets whatever the message below it names, which changes with the page: TRACK, PATTERN, STEPS, PULSES, OFFSET and so on
Picks the command printed beside it on the screen; which command that is depends on the page, and clicking the matching box on the screen does the same thing
Note — the expander works only touching the right edge of a FroeZe module. Attached, it takes that module's panel model and display brightness and lights its screens; detached, the screens go dark
Note — the euclidean page erases the selected track as soon as STEPS, PULSES or OFFSET is moved, and the auto-completion page can write over events already there. Save the pattern first.
Note — a track can be copied only onto a track of the same kind: an instrument track onto another instrument track, the accent track onto another accent track.
Note — this expander has no menu of its own beyond the licence line; the panel model and the sequencer's settings are on the FroeZe module's menu.
FroeZeX.notes: Source is not published. FroeZeXWidget::appendContextMenu at 0x1378d8 adds a separator and one MenuEntry carrying a string held on the widget, and no MenuItem at all, so there is nothing on this module's menu to write a line about. Param 0 is the continuous encoder at the centre of the panel; params 1 to 8 are the buttons the panel prints L1 to L4 and R1 to R4, which the manual describes as doing the same thing as the matching boxes on the touchscreen.

lines: A 14HP expander for the FroeZe sequencer, placed immediately to its left: it gives each of the fifteen instrument tracks its own swing CV input.
Sets the swing for that track alone by voltage, in place of the single swing FroeZe applies to the whole pattern
Note — a track's CV is read only after its box on the expander's screen is switched on with a left click. The boxes are drawn in one widget, so they cannot be reached by clicking for help.
Note — switching on even one track here disables FroeZe's own %SWING input: its LED turns red and the two-digit display below it shows two dashes.
Note — the expander works only when it touches the left edge of a FroeZe module, and it takes that module's panel model and display brightness.
Note — this expander has no menu of its own beyond the licence line; the panel model and the sequencer's settings are on the FroeZe module's menu.

lines: A clock source, clock modulator and low-frequency oscillator with eight independently programmable outputs, set up from a touchscreen and an encoder rather than from knobs.
Takes the outside clock and makes the module follow it, or acts as CV1 when the menu has reassigned this jack; a pulse counts on the way up past 2V and the input rearms below 0.1V
Starts and stops the clock, as a held gate or as a toggling trigger, unless the menu has turned this jack into CV2
Resets the master phase and the phase of all eight outputs when the menu has made this jack RESET; otherwise it is the CV3 modulation input
A modulation input, bipolar -5V/+5V unless its own screen page has been set to unipolar 0V/+10V or bipolar -10V/+10V; assign it to a parameter of any output from that output's pages
Carries the output of that channel: a pulse, triangle, sine, sample and hold, envelope or wavetable at the ratio set for it, or the gate, start or stop utility voltage
Turns to choose the highlighted item, move a value slider, or, with the menu switched off, set the tempo or the external clock mode
Starts and stops the clock
Confirms the highlighted item, ticks a checkbox, opens a value for editing, or enters the menu system
Leaves a value being edited, goes back one menu, and from the home menu switches the menu system off so the tempo can be changed
Note — a new module has outputs 1 to 4 at ratio x1 and outputs 5 to 8 off with red LEDs. Patching a cable into an off output sets it to x1; otherwise left-click its LED and choose a Modifier
Note — the input and output LEDs are buttons. A left click on one jumps the menu straight to that input's or that output's settings page.
Note — with the CLK jack empty the module is its own master, running from 1 BPM, printed as 0.02Hz, to 500Hz; tempo reads in BPM to 900 BPM and in Hz above. Turn the encoder while the display is blue
Note — with a cable in the CLK jack the module follows it by counted pulses, by one of thirteen PPQN settings from 2 to 192, or by a BPM-CV voltage; the encoder chooses which, with the menu off
Note — a CV does nothing until it is assigned, and nothing is assigned on a new module; one parameter of one output takes a single CV source, so mix several sources outside the module
Note — a jack set to carry the clock, or to run and stop the transport, is not a valid CV source, and the screen marks it with a red box or a blinking Not a CV message.
Note — the touchscreen is one widget, so no part of the menu system can be clicked for help. Some of it takes a touch: the page arrows and the quantizer page's note rotations ignore the encoder
Note — a left-side KX expander takes over the clock, run and reset duties and turns the first three jacks here into CV1, CV2 and CV3.
Menu — CLK/CV1 input: External clock input (default), CV1 input (bipolar -5V/+5V), CV1 input (unipolar 0V/+10V) — sets what the first jack is for
Menu — RUN/CV2 input: RUN/STOP toggle (default), Run while hi-gate, CV2 input (bipolar -5V/+5V), CV2 input (unipolar 0V/+10V) — sets what the second jack is for
Menu — CV3/RESET input: CV3 input (default bipolar -5V/+5V), CV3 input (unipolar 0V/+10V), RESET input (pulse resets phases) — sets what the third jack is for
Menu — RUN input (KX expander): RUN/STOP toggle (default), Run while hi-gate — sets whether the expander's run jack toggles on a trigger or runs while a gate is held; it appears when a KX is attached
Menu — Prefer frequency (Hz) rather than BPM — shows and edits the master rate in Hz at any speed, which also lowers the slowest setting to 0.02Hz
Menu — Output 8: Master phase (M.PHASE) 0V/+10V ramp up @ tempo — sends the master phase as a rising ramp from output 8, keeping that output's settings until the option is switched off

0.why: KlokSpidMkIIModule::process at 0x13ef68 compares the jack against 2.0 and at 0x13eff4 against 0x3dcccccd, which is 0.1; no setChannels anywhere in that function

1.why: same pair of thresholds, 0x13ef68 and 0x13eff4, walked for all eight inputs in one loop

3.why: docs/modules/KlokSpidMkII/Manual.md: CV4 to CV8 default to bipolar -5V/+5V, optionally unipolar 0V/+10V or bipolar -10V/+10V; the scaling at 0x13ef30 picks 0.05 when the low bound is -10 and 0.1 otherwise

KlokSpidMkII.notes: Source is not published. Read against docs/modules/KlokSpidMkII/Manual.md at tag v2.6.13 and against the unstripped binary. No family is given for the eight outputs: what a given output carries is whatever modifier and waveform has been programmed into it, from a clock pulse to an LFO to an envelope to a quantised pitch, so no one colour is true. The manual gives two different figures for the pulse thresholds, +2V rising with +0.1V falling in its voltage paragraph and +0.2V rising in the RUN and RESET paragraphs; the code settles it at 2V rising and 0.1V falling, the same pair for all three. Param 0 is the encoder and param 2 the SET button drawn on top of it, two pixels apart in the census; both can be clicked, because a click is resolved by which widget box contains the point and the button covers only its own centre. The menu also ends in a greyed License: full version (for everyone) label, which is not an item and gets no line.

lines: A 3HP expander for KlokSpid MkII, placed immediately to its left: it gives that module separate clock, run and reset jacks, and two offset voltages for its quantizers.
Takes the outside clock for KlokSpid MkII; a pulse counts on the way up past 2V and the input rearms below 0.1V
Starts and stops the clock, as a toggling trigger or while a gate is held, whichever the RUN input (KX expander) menu item names
A pulse resets KlokSpid MkII's master phase and the phase of all eight of its outputs
A bipolar -5V/+5V voltage added to an output's level before its quantizer rounds it to a note; which outputs take it is ticked on the KX Expander menu page, or by left-clicking this jack's LED
Note — attaching this expander turns KlokSpid MkII's first three jacks into CV1, CV2 and CV3, because the clock, run and reset duties move here; the displays above those jacks change to match
Note — a pre-offset does nothing on an output whose quantizer is switched off, meaning one with no note active on its piano.
Note — this expander has no menu of its own. Everything about it is set from KlokSpid MkII's touchscreen.

lines: A display: it reads a pitch and a gate and names what is being played, as a note, an interval or a chord, on a dot-matrix readout, and marks the notes on a circle of fifths. It has no outputs.
The notes to be named, at 1V per octave, one per polyphonic channel
Marks which of those notes are sounding: a channel counts while its gate is above 4.99V
Note — the readout stays on Need PITCH... or Need GATE... until both jacks are patched. A pitch on its own names nothing.
Note — the number of notes read is the smaller of the two channel counts, so a sixteen-channel pitch cable with a four-channel gate cable gives four notes.
Note — with nothing playing the readout shows Monophonic or the voice count of the cables patched.
Menu — Notation: English (C...A B), Latina (Do...La Si) — chooses whether note names are printed as letters or as Do, Re, Mi

KordZ.notes: Source is not published; read from the unstripped binary, since neither the README nor the repository has a KordZ manual at tag v2.6.13. The chord names come from KordZModule::SearchChordInDictionnary, whose literals run Unison, Octave, Minor, Major, Diminished, Augmented, Suspended 4, Maj(b5) and Chord? for anything it cannot name. The idle text Need PITCH... and Need GATE... and the voice-count text Monophonic and -voice poly. are literals in process and DisplayIdleMessage. The module's menu is Model, Notation and a greyed License: full version (for everyone) label; Model is the plugin-wide theme submenu and gets no line.

lines: Four independent sample-based drum voices in one 10HP panel: each channel plays one piece of a chosen vintage drum machine kit when triggered, and has its own audio output.
Fires that channel's drum sound; the trigger is taken on the way up past 1.7V and rearms below 0.2V
That channel's drum sound, mono
Selects that channel; pressing it on the channel already selected starts editing, and further presses step between the drum machine name and the kit piece. The encoder changes whichever one blinks
Sets the volume of the selected channel from 0% to 100% while nothing is blinking, and picks the drum machine or the kit piece while the channel is being edited
Note — an edit started with a channel button ends by itself after 30 seconds with no encoder or button movement.
Note — to hear a sound before choosing it, unpatch that channel's TRIG. jack. With the jack empty, selecting a drum machine or a kit piece plays it once; with a cable in it, that preview is off.
Note — the module reads only the first channel of a cable and sends one channel out, whatever the cable's width, because a drum hit needs no polyphony.
Note — without an OhmerPrems licence keyfile five of the sixteen drum machines sound: Oberheim DMX, Drumulator, LinnDrum, Roland 707 and 808. The rest select but stay silent, with a red channel LED

The +1.7V trigger minimum the README gives is confirmed exactly by the rescale constants at 0x1727e4, which also give the +0.2V release the README does not mention. lines: A four-oscillator digital VCO built on vector synthesis: A, B, C and D are drawn at the corners of a diamond and crossfaded by a joystick, by X and Y voltages, or by a timed mix envelope
The pitch of all four oscillators, at 1V per octave; the width of the cable patched here sets the polyphony
Selects the program by voltage, one step every +0.5V from +1V to +8.5V; anything below +1V is ignored and anything above +8.5V gives program 16
Moves the crossfade point sideways in the diamond, adding to the joystick position
Moves the crossfade point up and down in the diamond, adding to the joystick position
The modulating signal for the oscillators, used as linear through-zero FM or as phase modulation, whichever the program's FM page names; the depth is set there too
Starts the mix envelope on a gate of +1V or more and releases it when the gate falls back, and can retrigger the two LFOs
That oscillator on its own, before the crossfade unless its OSC VOLUME page has been set to post-joystick
The four oscillators crossfaded, which is the main output of vector synthesis
Turns to change whichever setting the screen is showing, including the waveform when an oscillator's first page is up
Steps to the next page of the current context, and returns to the first page when held with left Ctrl or left Command
Selects the setting printed beside it on the screen; left Ctrl or left Command with a press returns that setting to its default. On the mix envelope's first page it selects an envelope point
Selects that context and lights the red bar above it. Pressing the one already lit turns all five off, which is the PROGRAM context
Switches the mix envelope on and off for the current program
Note — the joystick is one widget rather than a control, so it cannot be clicked for help. Dragging it crossfades the four oscillators, and it sets the position of a mix envelope point being edited
Note — the module works in six contexts: A, B, C and D for the oscillators, MIX for the mix envelope, and PROGRAM when none of those five buttons is lit
Note — a program holds the four oscillators, the joystick position, the whole mix envelope, the FM depth and mode and both LFOs. Fifteen of the sixteen are Prophet VS programs, the sixteenth an INIT
Note — waveform 126 is SILENCE and switches that oscillator off; waveform 127 is WHITE NOISE, which has a fixed frequency and cannot be pitched or frequency-modulated.
Note — a WAVE file imported into a user slot must be 2048 samples, 16-bit signed PCM, mono, 44100Hz, and exactly 4140 bytes; anything else is refused.
Note — each imported user waveform is written into the patch as 8192 bytes of text. From the ninth the WARN./ERR. lamp blinks orange to warn that the patch file is growing; clear unused slots
Note — the WARN./ERR. lamp blinks red twice a second when a file operation fails, and the reason appears on the display until any button is pressed.
Note — a right-side VX expander brings the two LFOs, the joystick position and the mix envelope out as voltages.
Note — Randomize does nothing on this module.
Menu — Import .wav file as USER # — under User waveform, reads a WAVE file into the user slot the DATA ENTRY encoder is showing; a .wav file dropped on the panel does the same
Menu — Clear (free) USER # — under User waveform, empties the user slot now showing, and is greyed when that slot is already empty
Menu — Open from .vktMixEnv file — under MIX ENVelope, loads points, rates and loop into the current program; the envelope's on or off state is not part of the file
Menu — Save to .vktMixEnv file — under MIX ENVelope, writes the current points, rates and loop to a file
Menu — Reset to factory MIX ENVelope — under MIX ENVelope, puts the current program's envelope back to how the program shipped
Menu — Open from .vktProgram file — under Program #, loads a saved program into the current program number; the program takes its name from the filename
Menu — Save to .vktProgram file — under Program #, writes the current program to a file
Menu — Reset to factory program — under Program #, puts the current program back to the Prophet VS setting it shipped with
Menu — INITialize this program — under Program #, replaces the current program with the INIT settings
Note — the module is polyphonic to sixteen voices, and each of its six contexts has its own pages, stepped through with the PAGE button

Vektor.notes: Source is not published. Read against docs/modules/Vektor/Manual.md at tag v2.6.13, a long and careful manual, and against the unstripped binary. Every parameter is configured with an empty name; they are identified from the rendered panel and the manual's specification list, which names exactly the five context buttons A, B, C, D and MIX, the five left-side buttons, the PAGE button, the DATA ENTRY encoder and the ENV. button. The five left-side buttons are tagged to one line and the five context buttons to another, because within each group the button does the same job and the line is written about the one that was clicked. The joystick and the WARN./ERR. lamp are not parameters and have no census position, so they get no line and no tag; the joystick is covered by a Note because the module cannot be used without it. The Model (theme) submenu is the plugin-wide one and gets no line; Restore saved settings appears under both MIX ENVelope and Program # and is left out as self-explanatory.

lines: A 3HP expander for Vektor, placed immediately to its right: it brings the two LFOs, the joystick position and the mix envelope out as seven voltages.
Carries that LFO from Vektor as a -5V to +5V voltage; with the LFO switched off the jack holds 0V and its LED turns red
Reports the position of Vektor's physical joystick along that axis as a -5V to +5V voltage, taking no account of the X and Y input jacks or of the mix envelope
Goes to +10V while Vektor's mix envelope is running and 0V otherwise
Reports the mix envelope's position along that axis as a -5V to +5V voltage while the envelope runs; with the envelope off the jack holds 0V and all three lower LEDs turn red
Note — the expander works only when it touches the right edge of a Vektor module. With no link made, all seven LEDs blink red quickly.
Note — the envelope outputs leave out any offset from the joystick or from the X and Y input jacks.
Note — this expander has no menu of its own, and no controls; it takes its panel model from the Vektor it is attached to.

VX.notes: Source is not published. There is no VXWidget::appendContextMenu in the binary, which is why the README names this expander and KX as the two without a custom menu. The module is passive: no parameters, no inputs, and everything it sends is computed by the Vektor it is attached to. Polyphony is not claimed for the seven outputs: the manual does not say, and the writing path is inside VektorModule::process rather than in any VX code, so nothing here settles it.

Sets how far the LFO modulates pitch
Sets how far the LFO modulates amplitude
Sets the rate of that segment of the pitch envelope
Sets the level that segment of the pitch envelope moves to
Sets how far the modulation wheel and aftertouch reach the pitch through the LFO
Transposes the whole voice
Sets how much of the feedback operator's output is fed back into itself
Sets the level of the master output
The whole voice, mixed to one mono signal
That operator on its own
The pitch envelope as a voltage
The LFO as a voltage
Note — no sound in this build: process sets the channel counts on the nine outputs and writes no voltage to them. The maker's README says the phase-modulation engine is written but not switched on
Note — the module is marked hidden in the installed plugin.json, so it is not listed in Rack's module browser at all. It can only reach a rack inside a patch that already has one.
Note — the large display is one widget, so nothing shown on it can be reached by clicking for help. The two encoders and the two buttons above it are what work it.
Note — the voice is edited in a bank of 32. Saving a voice writes it back into the bank, and the bank can be read from and written to DX7 system exclusive files or the maker's own cartridge files.
Note — the maker reports that on some Mac machines the panel artwork fails to draw at certain zoom levels.
Menu — Import DX7 (32-voice "VMEM" or single-voice "VCED") SysEx file... — under File, reads a DX7 bank or single voice into the module
Menu — Export to 32-voice DX7 "VMEM" SysEx file... — under File, writes all 32 voices out as a DX7 bank dump
Menu — Export VOICE # to single-voice DX7 "VCED" SysEx file... — under File, writes the voice now showing out on its own
Menu — Open ".6opdx" cartridge file — under File, reads all 32 voices from one of the maker's own cartridge files
Menu — Save all 32 voices to ".6opdx" cartridge file as... — under File, writes the whole bank to one of the maker's own cartridge files
Menu — LCD/OLED emulation: Genuine LCD, Backlit LCD retrofit, OLED retrofit — chooses how the module's display is drawn

6OPDX.notes: Source is not published, and there is no manual: docs/modules/6OP-DX/Manual.md at tag v2.6.13 is a nine-line placeholder saying the manual will be written for a later version. The entry is built from the census parameter names, which are unusually complete here, from the rendered panel, and from the binary. The parameter names and the module's own SysEx import and export fix the semantics exactly: SixOpDXModule::importSysEx, exportVMEM and exportVCED read and write DX7 VMEM and VCED voice data, so each control is the DX7 voice parameter its name gives, and the lines describe those without quoting any figure, because no range was read. Twenty-nine parameter indices have no widget position at all and are left untagged and unwritten. THE MODULE PRODUCES NO SOUND: the outputs are only ever resized, never written, which matches the README's statement that the PM engine is not yet enabled. IT IS ALSO HIDDEN: the installed plugin.json marks this model "hidden": true, so it does not appear in the module browser. That is the one thing in this plugin's model registration that would keep a model out of the browser, and no other model carries the flag.
